scope: Theorem 6.1 (Two-sided correlation) of the manuscript “The Poisson-Dirichlet law for prime predecessors” (preprints/The-Poisson-Dirichlet-Law-for-Prime-Predecessors-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 011 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 4b54d35506a19280), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 40. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix d ≥ 1, ε > 0, and intervals I1, . . . , Id whose lower endpoints are at least xε and whose upper endpoints have product at most x1−ε. Let l = (l1, . . . , ld) run over ordered tuples of distinct primes with li ∈ Ii, and put l := l1 · · · ld, Cx := X l 1 l , Fx(n) := W(n) X l 1l|n − Cx ! . (6.4) Suppose G(n) = G(n∗) and |G(n)| ≤ LCτ(n∗)C, for fixed C. For every fixed smooth compactly supported Ψ : (0, ∞) → C and every fixed A > 0, X w≥1 Ψ(w/x) w Fx(w)G(w + 1)W1(w)W1(w + 1) ≪A L−A . (6.5) The constants and sufficiently-large-x threshold may depend on all the fixed data, including the fixed inert bands, but the estimate is uniform over the active groups and slot intervals satisfying the stated bounds. The slots have no joint restriction other than distinctness.
